title: Minimum Operations to Make Binary Array Elements Equal to One II
summary: Given a binary array nums, you can perform the following operation any number of times: Choose any index i and flip all elements from index i to the end of the array.
statement: Given a binary array nums, you can perform the following operation any number of times: Choose any index i and flip all elements from index i to the end of the array. Flipping an element means changing its value from 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0. Determine the minimum number of operations required to make all elements in nums equal to 1.
constraints: nums is a nonempty binary array.
An operation chooses an index and flips every element from it through the end.
Return the minimum operations needed to make all elements one.
hints: Only the parity of prior suffix flips affects the current bit.
Scan left to right; when the effective bit is zero, a flip at this index is forced and toggles parity.
If value xor parity equals zero, increment operations and parity xor equals one.
Later flips cannot repair a current zero without also beginning here or earlier, so each greedy flip is necessary and sufficient.
editorial: Later flips cannot repair a current zero without also beginning here or earlier, so each greedy flip is necessary and sufficient.

tests.explanation: The required effective bits alternate at four boundaries, so four suffix flips are necessary.
Every bit is already one, so no operation is needed.
